rows.subject: E_AMMO (Ammo): custom touch
rows.notes: +5 with one-time hint; consumed by shooting

rows.subject: E_BEAR (Bear): custom tick+touch
rows.notes: draws nothing at all; both sensitivity branches, the E_BREAKABLE attack only bears make, death by a player bullet for score (ORCLFIRE), and duplicator-spawned copies that inherit the source stat (ORCLHUNT)

rows.subject: E_BLINK_RAY_EW (unnamed): default draw/tick/touch
rows.notes: lit ray blocks the player; destroys a Destructible tile in its path and takes the square

rows.subject: E_BLINK_RAY_NS (unnamed): default draw/tick/touch
rows.notes: includes the ported ELEMENTS.PAS:845-848 push bug (ZZT-QUIRK in elements.go), pinned by the pushed-into-wall checkpoint

rows.subject: E_BLINK_WALL (Blink wall): custom draw+tick
rows.notes: P1 start delay and P2 period; lays, damages, retracts

rows.subject: E_BOARD_EDGE (unnamed): custom touch
rows.notes: refusal with no neighbor; transfer with a neighbor board

rows.subject: E_BOMB (Bomb): custom draw+tick+touch
rows.notes: armed by touch, pushed while armed; blast radius pinned on the ellipse boundary. No checkpoint falls between the two explosion phases, whose breakable colours are Random(7)

rows.subject: E_BOULDER (Boulder): custom touch
rows.notes: pushed alone, in a chain, and refused; crushes a Destructible blocker, refused by a breakable

rows.subject: E_BREAKABLE (Breakable): default draw/tick/touch
rows.notes: inert on touch; destroyed by a bullet

rows.subject: E_BULLET (Bullet): custom tick+touch
rows.notes: flight, water, both perpendicular ricochets, enemy-vs-player damage, player-vs-creature damage and score, and bullet-vs-bullet ownership are oracle-backed (ORCLFIRE). Self-shot suppression is the friendly-fire deviation. M16.5a closed the point-blank half: BoardShoot's ownership test now carries GAME.PAS:1246's sense, and ORCLFIRE's Blank Bay pins a player point-blanking a monster in two axes (pb-east, pb-south) and an enemy point-blanking the player (pb-point-blank). The OBJECT/SCROLL `SHOT` send a spent bullet makes is OOP, covered by M16.6

rows.subject: E_CENTIPEDE_HEAD (Head): custom tick+touch
rows.notes: P1 0/P2 0 make both alignment gates and the deviance gate unsatisfiable, and a one-wide corridor makes the blocked-path perpendicular draw irrelevant; covers follower adoption, both dead-end reversals, and promote-then-attack

rows.subject: E_CENTIPEDE_SEGMENT (Segment): custom tick+touch
rows.notes: the whole proc is the Leader countdown; reached by cutting a train in half with a damaging touch, after which the orphaned rear wakes into a head

rows.subject: E_CONVEYOR_CCW (Counter): custom draw+tick
rows.notes: animation and cycle gate from ORCLDEV; a ring broken by a solid square from ORCLRIDE

rows.subject: E_CONVEYOR_CW (Clockwise): custom draw+tick
rows.notes: animation and cycle gate from ORCLDEV; a free ring carrying a boulder and a gem from ORCLRIDE

rows.subject: E_DOOR (Door): custom touch
rows.notes: matching key opens; missing key refuses

rows.subject: E_DUPLICATOR (Duplicator): custom draw+tick
rows.notes: all five branches: copy, push-then-copy, recursive push, refusal, and touching the source for a player standing on the destination

rows.subject: E_ENERGIZER (Energizer): custom touch
rows.notes: pickup/warning melodies and post-expiry state; no checkpoint while energized (flash color derives from vanilla-randomized CurrentTick the engine pins — scenario-design exclusion)

rows.subject: E_FAKE (Fake): custom touch
rows.notes: walk-through with one-time message

rows.subject: E_FOREST (Forest): custom touch
rows.notes: clears with message and sound

rows.subject: E_GEM (Gem): custom touch
rows.notes: counters via oracle sidebar

rows.subject: E_INVISIBLE (Invisible): custom touch
rows.notes: hidden in the initial capture, revealed to a normal wall on touch

rows.subject: E_KEY (Key): custom touch
rows.notes: pickup and duplicate-key refusal

rows.subject: E_LINE (Line): custom draw
rows.notes: neighbor-joined line characters compared in the board captures

rows.subject: E_LION (Lion): custom tick+touch
rows.notes: P1 9 forces the seek half of `P1 < Random(10)`; charges and attacks down the player row (ORCLBEAST), flees the same row while the player is energized and is eaten for score (ORCLHUNT)

rows.subject: E_MESSAGE_TIMER (unnamed): custom tick
rows.notes: message text, position, flash phase (P2), and expiry compared against the oracle

rows.subject: E_MONITOR (Monitor): custom tick

rows.subject: E_SPINNING_GUN (Spinning gun): custom draw+tick
rows.notes: rotation from ORCLDEV; both aim branches firing from ORCLRIDE, with p1 8 / p2 9 forcing both random draws so the outcome is RNG-free. M16.5a adds the third case, from ORCLFIRE's Blank Bay: a gun in the player's own ROW, whose vertical shot has delta Signum(0)=0 and lands on its own square. Vanilla refuses it and falls through to the horizontal shot, which point-blanks the player for 10 a tick while the gun survives (pb-point-blank, pb-gun-alive) — under the inverted ownership test the gun destroyed itself instead

rows.subject: 'H' help window: TextWindowDisplayFile('GAME.HLP', 'Playing ZZT')
rows.notes: The engine's HelpEvent carries only a filename/title (M3.9); the adapter loads GAME.HLP itself via TextWindowOpenFile, the function the interactive path also calls, and compares its first page against the oracle's window (PARITY.md oracle-modal-scroll normalization). GAME.HLP's '$Getting Started.' heading line surfaced a real gap in oracleWindowCaption, which stripped only '!label;' captions — generalized to also strip a '$' heading and a ':label;' line per TXTWIND.PAS TextWindowDrawLine. The title screen's high-score LIST view (Engine.HighScoresDisplay) has no scenario here: it is drawn only by the terminal-only GameTitleLoop (engine/zzt.go), never by GameStepWithInputs or the protocol — confirmed by grep, see TestOracleParityPromptScenario's doc comment and NOTES.md. Its actually-reachable surfaces are already tracked separately: mode.modal-highscore (M16.9), input.title-highscores (M16.11), service.high-scores (M16.15).

rows.subject: GamePromptEndPlay / SidebarPromptYesNo: the 'Q'/Escape "End this game?" yes/no prompt
rows.notes: Oracle-verified via the sidebar-prompt-line normalization (PARITY.md oracle-sidebar-prompt-line): the real ZZT's fixed "End this game? " line at (63,5) is asserted against the capture text, since the headless engine only emits QuitPromptEvent and draws nothing there itself. Declining with N is proven a no-op (SubmitQuitReply(false), matching its own doc comment) by a follow-up move that still succeeds with unchanged counters. Confirming with Y (GamePlayExitRequested/QuitEvent) is not re-verified here — that effect is unit-tested elsewhere, and the vanilla return-to-title screen it triggers is already oracle-certified as the boot/title checkpoint every M16.3-M16.7 scenario shares.

rows.subject: Portable .ZZT/.SAV world-file round trip; malformed/truncated input is refused everywhere untrusted bytes reach the loader, never panics
rows.notes: BoardOpen/worldReadFrom had no bounds checking (RLE run count, StatCount vs MAX_STAT, board count vs MAX_BOARD); LoadWorldBytes/LoadPristineWorld/RoomManager.LoadWorld/RestoreSnapshot and WorldLoad now validate every board once (validateWorldBoards, game.go) before it can reach a real BoardOpen, closing a live-server-crash gap on the multiplayer upload/host/restore path. .SAV is the same GameWorldSave routine as .ZZT (game.go) with darkness/torch/time state proven round-tripped. .BRD export/import + malformed-input refusal (editor_session_test.go, safeBoardOpen) predate this task and are exercised by service.editor-solo (M16.13); board re-entry/entry-point (elem.board-edge, M16.3) and title-screen animation (elem.monitor, M16.3) were already oracle-certified and only gained one strengthened return-trip checkpoint here (pass.scn).

deviations.title: Death is a respawn (penalty + brief invulnerability), not game-over
Overlapping players: the arriver is pushed to a free adjacent square
Multiplayer projectile/contact damage follows an explicit friendly-fire policy
Modals freeze only the acting player; the room keeps ticking
World.Info.Flags are shared across players (co-op puzzle progress)
A restored snapshot drops other players; a joiner arrives fresh
Per-player keys/inventory live in an account sidecar, not the snapshot
The menu omits vanilla's S game-speed — the server owns the tick
A high score is entered on quit, not on death
Movement is arrows + numpad 8/4/6/2 only; WASD removed (S collides with save)
Pickup/shot/damage sounds are per-acting-player; #play stays room-wide
A windowed scroll is consumed on reply, not on touch (de-modal)
Presentation-only additions with no vanilla counterpart (name popup, picker, overlay, chat, sound UI, Dream, help/debug windows)
Mobile ships text entry only; touch gameplay is a filed gap task (M16.18a)
